title: हवालात
logline: Branch A, the first hour after the vote: Nandini arrests Nirala by the book, locks him in her own thana's cobwebbed lockup, and at ten past twelve lets eight hundred sacks leave town on her own SHO's stamp. From behind the bars her prisoner tells her how to fight back, and the first door she knocks on shuts in her face.
language_note: Hinglish: Hindi in Devanagari, English words in Latin script, in the same line.

characters.name: नंदिनी जोशी (Nandini Joshi)
characters.role: LEAD. Sub-Inspector, Imlipur thana, six weeks into her first posting. Tonight she chose the book.
characters.look: Indian woman, 28, tall (about 170 cm), lean, very straight-backed, long neck. Medium-brown skin, oval face, straight thick black eyebrows, level dark-brown eyes, a firm mouth. Black hair, clean centre parting, low ponytail to the shoulder blades; no fringe, no loose strands. No make-up, no bindi, no jewellery, no watch. Approved force uniform, crisp: sandy khaki shirt with two buttoned chest pockets, full sleeves; dark teal epaulettes with TWO off-white bars; white lantern on a round teal patch on each upper sleeve; khaki trousers; black belt with a black handcuff pouch on her right hip (empty in this episode: the cuffs are on Nirala); black shoes; blue ballpoint pen in her left chest pocket. No cap, no stars. Cherry-red open-face helmet: on the lobby bench in b1 and b2, under her left arm from b3 (set down on the SHO's desk in b4, picked up in b5, in her left hand in b6 and b7; set down by the doorway in b8 and never in frame again); no helmet in frame from b8 on (D-016 direction 19).
characters.voice_note: Female, late twenties, clear mid-range voice. Educated small-city north-Indian Hindi with crisp English police words. Quick and clipped by habit; in this episode she is under pressure the whole time, so she is quieter, slower and more exact, never louder. Dry, not sarcastic. Her lines at the crossing (l08 to l11) are said like entries in a diary, not like a lament.

characters.name: सुधीर निराला (Sudhir Nirala)
characters.role: The man who ran the fake thana. Under arrest from the first second, in his own uniform.
characters.look: Indian man, 40, slight and short (about 160 cm), narrow sloping shoulders, thin neck. Light-brown skin, long narrow face, large earnest eyes, neat black pencil moustache. Home-stitched copy of the force uniform, over-starched and ONE SIZE TOO BIG: shoulder seams drooping, sleeves to the knuckles, collar standing off the neck, belt tail hanging loose. Teal epaulettes with three off-white bars; lantern sleeve patches. The only peaked cap in the series (khaki, teal band, shiny black peak, no badge), dead level, never taken off. Big blank brass-yellow medal on a maroon-and-off-white striped ribbon above his left chest pocket. Empty brown leather holster on his right hip from b2 on. Plain steel handcuffs on BOTH wrists from b1 to the end of the episode.
characters.voice_note: Male, forty, light careful tenor. Small-town north-Indian Hindi in an official register, English police terms said with great care. Courteous, never raises his voice, never jokes. Frightened tonight: a thin, steady voice, not a stammer. When he gets the idea in b9 he is still quiet but firmer, a clerk who knows the procedure.

characters.name: पुष्पा कुमारी (Pushpa Kumari)
characters.role: Head Constable, twenty-six years at the Imlipur thana. Has kept the second almirah key for two years.
characters.look: Indian woman, 50, short (about 152 cm) and solid. Wheat-brown skin, round face, sharp small eyes over round steel-rimmed spectacles worn low. Grey-streaked black hair in a tight high bun with two steel knitting needles crossed through it. Approved force uniform with ONE off-white bar on teal epaulettes, lantern patches, khaki trousers, black shoes. Over it a hand-knitted plum-purple cardigan, open, two sagging pockets; a ball of orange wool in the right pocket. Cloth knitting bag over her left shoulder outdoors. No cap.
characters.voice_note: Female, fifty, low, dry, even alto. Plain, economical small-town Hindi. Never surprised; warmth shows only as dryness. Her two jokes in this episode (l06, l24) are said completely straight.

characters.name: रामसेवक (Ramsevak)
characters.role: The first complainant from the red file. One shot, one line, never recurs as a face.
characters.look: Thin man, 50s, grey stubble, white vest, a shawl pulled round him, seen through a wooden door open a hand's width at 1 a.m.
characters.voice_note: Tired, flat, older male. One line, not hostile: a man who has finished with hoping. Fully voiced, not whispered; it is the episode's last line.

location: Four of the seven series plates: talkies_lobby (b1, b2), crossing_stall (b3, b6, b7), real_thana (b4, b5, b8, b9, b10), lane_doorway (b11). Fictional town of Imlipur, a railway line cutting it in two. All night, no crowd.
time_of_day: Night: 11 p.m. in b1, midnight in b5, ten past twelve in b7, 1 a.m. in b11. Clocks are painted with hands and no numerals; every time that matters is spoken.

He crosses the line to the real thana for the first time.

The real thana at night, one tube light. Shot 1: at the back, the cobwebbed barred door of the lockup; Pushpa's hands fight a rusted padlock, a cobweb across the bars, Nandini behind her as a back, setting her red helmet down on the SHO's desk; l06 plays over it. sfx_notes: Bed, b1 and b2: the shut talkies at night, a big empty room: faint ceiling creak, one moth ticking against the bare bulb, crickets outside the high windows.
b1: handcuff ratchet on frame one, close and dry, two clicks (one per wrist). Nothing else under it for the first second.
b2: cloth bag drawstring; a match strike and the soft drip of wax; pen scratch on the tag under l05; after the lines, a bulb switch click and the room tone drops as the light goes.
b3: footsteps on railway ballast (three rhythms: long even strides, short brisk steps, small careful steps with a faint clink of steel cuffs); the signal relay ticking; crickets. No train.
Bed, b4, b5, b8 to b10: the real thana at night: tube-light hum, slow ceiling fan, a far dog once in b8.
b4: a rusted padlock grinding and refusing under l06, then giving; the barred door swinging shut, one heavy iron clang that ends the beat. Keep the clang clear of l06.
b5: the wall clock tick, one tick louder as the hands meet; footsteps leaving; the helmet lifted off the desk.

b6: diesel truck idling, close and low, with headlight glare as a faint electrical hum. Duck the engine right down under l08 ('रोकिए। काग़ज़ दिखाइए।'): it is Glimpse A's last line and must be fully intelligible. Paper rustle as the slip changes hands; keep the idle low under l09 and l10.

b7: the gate arm creaking up; the truck going into gear and pulling away over the rails (wheels thudding the track twice), the engine fading into the distance under l11, which sits on the fade, not on the gear change. Then crickets.
b8: tube-light hum; a soft brush of cloth as his hand goes to his collar.

b9: the bench creaks as he stands; cuff chain against an iron bar once, on the cut to shot 2 between l17 and l18, not under either line. Pushpa's needles click under l17 and l18 and stop dead before l19.

b10: padlock click, almirah door groaning open, a dull thump and a breath of dust as the register comes out; one page turn under l25. Two knocks on wood in the silence after l25, as a pre-lap into b11.

b11: night lane: a far dog, a moth at the wall lamp. The chain latch rattles taut as the door stops a hand's width open, before l26. After l27 has finished, the door shuts and the bolt is shot: solid, close, then near silence for the hold. Nothing loud sits on l27; the bed is down to almost nothing under it.
music_note: No music from b1 to b6: the arrest and the lockup are played on room sound. One low, sustained string note enters under the tail-lights in b7 and holds through l11; it is gone by the first line of b8. Silence again in b8. From l17 in b9 a light, dry plucked figure (the series' caper motif, slowed) enters very quietly and builds a little under the key and the register in b10. It stops dead on the second knock in the pre-lap. b11 has no music; the door shut and the hold play on silence. Instrumental, no melody line over dialogue, no percussion hits.
ending_question: The people of Imlipur trusted a fake uniform and were turned away by the real one, so how can she get even one complainant to put a thumb in the register before the microphones go up at ten?

Tags: [calm], [quietly], [sharply], [nervous] and [sighs] were used in the proof scenes. [hesitant] (l03, l21), [deadpan] (l06, l23), [flatly] (l11, l16, l25) and [earnest] (l18, l22) are in the skill's verify group and are not yet confirmed for any Series 2 voice: if a voice ignores one, S10 swaps [hesitant] for [quietly], [deadpan] or [flatly] for [calm], and [earnest] for [calm]. It is Glimpse A's last line and has to project over the diesel idle, unlike the rest of her quiet episode.

Short-turn flags for the voice director: l02 'जी, madam।' (10 characters) is a whole line by D-016 direction 11 and cannot be merged; record extra takes. l12 and l22 are under 20 characters and l25 is 20; each carries a word that makes it stable.

Words kept the same throughout: मोहर for the stamp, sign for the signature, ताला for a lock, चाबी for the key, मुलज़िम for the prisoner, register for the FIR register, almirah in Latin script as in the bible. No bare 'साहब': always 'SHO साहब'. Nobody calls Nirala 'Inspector' in this episode. No यह or वह.

Props and their state: handcuffs on both Nirala's wrists, b1 to b9. The wooden revolver is lying in profile in b2 and is then sealed in a cloth bag; it is never pointed. The red-cloth file goes with Pushpa in b2, is on the SHO's desk in b9 and under Nandini's arm in b11. The green register comes out of the almirah in b10 and in b11 is held flat against her chest by her left arm, with the red file under the same arm; her right hand knocks and stays half raised. The helmet is set down by the doorway in b8 and is not seen again. The orange-wool key appears in b10. The pink slip is painted blank with ov_slip_signature, and l09 speaks the signature. The medal and the cap stay on Nirala throughout. The truck driver is a forearm only; he has no face and no line.
